ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, the moving point P starts from vertex A of the rectangle ABCD, and moves uniformly along the direction A→B→C on the sides AB, BC at a speed of $1\, \text{cm/s}$ to point C. The area $S$ ($\text{cm}^{2}$) of $\triangle APC$ as a function of the movement time $t$ (s) is illustrated in the figure. What is the length of AB?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that point P moves from point A to B, the distance S increases with time t. When point P moves from point B to C, S decreases as t increases.\\
Therefore, based on Graph 2, the duration of point P's movement from B to C is 4s,\\
Since the speed of point P is 1cm/s,\\
Thus, $BC=1\times4=4$ (cm),\\
Given that when point P moves along the line AB reaching point B, the area of $\triangle APC$ is at its maximum,\\
Hence, from Graph 2: the area of $\triangle APC$ is $6\text{cm}^{2}$,\\
Therefore, the area of $\triangle ABC$, ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC=6$,\\
Thus, $AB=\boxed{3}$cm.

The area $S$ ($\text{cm}^{2}$) of $\triangle APC$ as a function of the movement time $t$ (s) is illustrated in the figure. What is the length of AB?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that point P moves from point A to B, the distance S increases with time t. When point P moves from point B to C, S decreases as t increases.\\
Therefore, based on Graph 2, the duration of point P's movement from B to C is 4s,\\
Since the speed of point P is 1cm/s,\\
Thus, $BC=1\times4=4$ (cm),\\
Given that when point P moves along the line AB reaching point B, the area of $\triangle APC$ is at its maximum,\\
Hence, from Graph 2: the area of $\triangle APC$ is $6\text{cm}^{2}$,\\
Therefore, the area of $\triangle ABC$, ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC=6$,\\
Thus, $AB=\boxed{3}$cm

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In Figure 1, ABCD is a rectangle, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right, point P is located on side AB and moves along the path A→B→C; AC and PC are also drawn in the figure. Figure 2 is the relationship graph of S and t, the vertical axis is S/cm^2, the horizontal axis is t/s, the graph rises linearly from the origin to the peak value 6, corresponding to time t=a, and then decreases linearly to 0, corresponding to time t=a+4.
Then reason: When P moves from A to B, the area of △APC gradually increases; when P moves from B to C, the area gradually decreases. Therefore the descending segment of the graph represents P moving from B to C, and the time used is (a+4)-a=4 seconds. The speed of point P is 1 cm/s, so BC=1×4=4 cm. The peak value of the graph occurs when P reaches B; at this time △APC is △ABC, with area 6 cm^2. In a rectangle, the area of △ABC is 1/2×AB×BC, so 1/2×AB×4=6, solving gives AB=3 cm.
